status: Scoped source implementation verified; coordinated desktop and packaged acceptance are separate gates.
scope: Persistent local calendar editing, recurrence and timezone handling, local scheduling messages and a bounded offline outbox. No provider reads, invitation sends or user notifications are performed by these workflows.
implementedScopes: Exclusive local SQLite calendar stores with revision checks, bounded imports, event details, editing and reopening persisted data.
All 597 names and aliases in the pinned published timezone dataset; embedded VTIMEZONE definitions take precedence per document.
Explicit ambiguous and nonexistent local-time choices, floating and all-day display-zone filtering, and historical second offsets.
All seven RFC recurrence frequencies with bounded expansion, rule-generated gap skipping, RDATE periods, stable instance identities and detached exceptions.
UID and recurrence-instance create, update, delete, attendee response, local REQUEST/REPLY/CANCEL application and stale-message checks.
Unknown ICS properties, parameters and components retained during supported changes; no-op export retains the original source, including a BOM.
A local pending outbox with payload quotas, attempt fencing, reconnect recovery and an explicitly invoked filesystem-only test transport.
Atomic file publication with destination fingerprints, held calendar writer transactions and explicit errors when file publication succeeds but origin metadata cannot commit.
Suite CLI commands for timezone diagnostics, persistent calendars, agenda, details, edits, scheduling-message import, export and local outbox inspection.

coverage: Every published zone name resolves in winter and summer; this is availability coverage, not an independent accuracy oracle for every transition.

Independent expected instants and offsets for Toronto folds and gaps, Lord Howe's half-hour change, Samoa's skipped day, Kathmandu, Chatham, Dublin, aliases, reversed-sign Etc names and historical New York seconds.
Export and reopen generated and embedded timezone definitions, including authoritative custom zones during full-form edits.
DST recurrence COUNT, RDATE periods, floating/all-day ranges, invalid dates, moved and cancelled instances, future ranges and preserved source extensions.
Real SQLite revision conflicts, source/outbox rollback on quotas, stale scheduling messages, organizer and attendee checks, and persisted local outbox attempts.

An independent SQLite writer is blocked during asynchronous publication; a changed destination is preserved with rescue bytes; a later metadata commit failure reports that the file was already exported.

cliCalendarAndHelp.qualification: This source-level CLI run preceded the final narrow core preservation fixes; those fixes are covered by the final 60-case core run. The CLI source was subsequently formatted without a behavior change.

timezoneProvider.qualification: Coverage follows the exact finite data shipped by this pinned provider. Future political timezone changes require a deliberate dependency and data update.

bounds.behavior: Limits fail explicitly and preserve the previously stored source. Caller-specified result, iteration and time budgets apply in addition to these defaults.

remainingGatesAndLimits: The synchronous ICAL iterator cannot be interrupted inside an individual next() call. Untrusted desktop operations must use the separately implemented isolated calendar worker; its process deadlines, cancellation and orphan tests have their own evidence.
Coordinated desktop calendar workflows, full candidate builds and packaged acceptance remain owned by the final coordinator; this record does not certify their completion.

No live OAuth account connection, provider write, invitation delivery or server acknowledgement has been accepted. A delivered filesystem-test item means only that the explicit local test transport completed.
Unsupported series changes with detached overrides and unsupported this-and-future rule or timezone changes are refused instead of silently rewriting source semantics.
This implementation is not a claim of full RFC 5545/5546 interoperability, shared-calendar collaboration, alarm execution or Office/Outlook parity.

Atomic file replacement has no operating-system compare-and-swap guarantee against an uncooperative writer between the final fingerprint check and rename. Cooperating calendar writers are fenced by the SQLite transaction.
Candidate signing, production readiness and clean-machine acceptance require separate release review.
